Marking input events as handled has no effect on the entered/exited signals, only if input events are sent, like [`_input_event`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_collisionobject2d.html#class-collisionobject2d-private-method-input-event), which handles unhandled events

Changing this unconditionally would be a major compatibility breakage as it's expected to work

clear.

If i need the node response mouse enter that effacted by Viewport.set_input_as_handled, i must implemented it with _input() by myself ? 
Is there a best practice for this situation？

Can confirm that a `Control` with input mode set to `Stop` will block input correctly, but the act of setting something as handled causes the mouse event to propagate differently, unsure exactly what is going on here

I suspect this might be because input is grabbed before it reaches the `Control`, which causes it to not block anything, so this might or might not be a bug, unsure

Further testing would be needed, I suspect that if you use another `Control` instead of a `Node2D` for `B` this will behave differently, you should also try to accept the event inside the `Control`

So not sure if this is a bug or if it's expected, needs more testing by people knowing more about input

CC @Sauermann any thoughts?

> I wrote a script to adapt this issue. Paste here. If anyone need a interactable Area2D, may it can come in handy
> 
> 
> ```
> extends Area2D
> class_name ControlArea
> 
> ## signal when mouse entered any shape of this Area2D
> signal touch_start()
> ## signal when mouse exited all shape of this Area2D
> signal touch_end()
> ## when left mouse button click any shape of this Area2D
> signal click_left()
> ## when right mouse button click any shape of this Area2D
> signal click_right()
> ## when left mouse button pressed and moved
> signal pick_up()
> ## if pick up before, release left mouse button will trigger put_down() instead of click_left()
> signal put_down()
> ## When dragging, the current position of the mouse; Unscaled mouse position, relative to the previous position in the screen coordinate system (previous frame position).
> signal dragging(global_position:Vector2, screen_relative:Vector2)
> 
> ## PASS: The current Area2D will not prevent the event from continuing to propagate
> ## STOP: The current Area2D will prevent events from continuing to propagate on the sence tree
> ## IGNORE: The current Area2D will not respond to any events
> @export
> var filter:Control.MouseFilter = Control.MouseFilter.MOUSE_FILTER_PASS
> 
> var _last_mouse_position:Vector2
> var _temp = Object.new()
> var _is_mouse_in := false
> var _is_emit_mouse_in := false
> var _global_position_on_pick_up:Vector2
> var _is_left_press := false
> var _left_press_msec := 0
> var _is_dragged = false:
> 	set(v):
> 		if _is_dragged != v:
> 			_is_dragged = v
> 			if v:
> 				pick_up.emit()
> 			else:
> 				put_down.emit()
> 	get():
> 		return _is_dragged
> 
> func _ready() -> void:
> 	get_viewport().physics_object_picking_sort = true
> 
> func _process(delta: float) -> void:
> 	if _is_left_press:	
> 		if Input.is_mouse_button_pressed(MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT):
> 			var n = get_viewport().get_mouse_position()
> 			if n == _last_mouse_position:
> 				pass
> 			else:
> 				_is_dragged = true
> 				dragging.emit(n, n - _last_mouse_position)
> 				_last_mouse_position = n
> 		else:
> 			_is_left_press = false
> 
> func _mouse_enter() -> void:
> 	_is_mouse_in = true
> 
> func _mouse_exit() -> void:
> 	_is_mouse_in = false
> 	if _is_emit_mouse_in:
> 		touch_end.emit()
> 		_is_emit_mouse_in = false
> 
> func _input_event(viewport: Viewport, event: InputEvent, shape_idx: int) -> void:
> 	if filter == Control.MouseFilter.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP and event.get_meta("stop_area", _temp) == _temp:
> 		event.set_meta("stop_area", self)
> 	if event.get_meta("stop_area", _temp) != _temp and event.get_meta("stop_area") != self:
> 		return
> 		
> 	if event is InputEventMouseMotion:
> 		if filter == Control.MouseFilter.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP:
> 			if event.get_meta("stop_area", _temp) == self:
> 				if _is_mouse_in and !_is_emit_mouse_in:
> 					touch_start.emit()
> 					_is_emit_mouse_in = true
> 			else:
> 				if _is_mouse_in and _is_emit_mouse_in:
> 					touch_end.emit()
> 					_is_emit_mouse_in = false
> 		elif filter == Control.MouseFilter.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE:
> 			return
> 		elif filter == Control.MouseFilter.MOUSE_FILTER_PASS:
> 			if _is_mouse_in and !_is_emit_mouse_in:
> 				touch_start.emit()
> 				_is_emit_mouse_in = true
> 	elif event is InputEventMouseButton:
> 		if filter == Control.MouseFilter.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP and event.get_meta("stop_area", _temp) != self:
> 			return
> 		elif filter == Control.MouseFilter.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE:
> 			return
> 		if event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_RIGHT and !event.pressed:
> 			click_right.emit()
> 		elif event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT and event.pressed:
> 			_last_mouse_position = get_viewport().get_mouse_position()
> 			_is_left_press = true
> 			_left_press_msec = Time.get_ticks_msec()
> 		elif event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT and !event.pressed:
> 			if _is_left_press:
> 				_is_left_press = false
> 				if !_is_dragged or (Time.get_ticks_msec() - _left_press_msec < 100 and _last_mouse_position.distance_to(get_viewport().get_mouse_position()) < 20):
> 					click_left.emit()
> 				_is_dragged = false
> 	
> ```
